extracted.intended_audience: regulated entities, state and local air agencies, environmental stakeholders, attorneys, and members of the public tracking federal environmental rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: API listing of Federal Register documents related to environmental protection (EPA, NRC, DOT, etc.), containing abstracts that summarize proposed rules, final rules, and related regulatory actions. Useful for stakeholders monitoring SIP actions, NAAQS determinations, NESHAP/NESHAP reviews, SNURs, delegation requests, and other federal environmental actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SIP approval — noninterference with CAA requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: “EPA is proposing to approve ... This action ... as it will not interfere with any applicable requirement concerning attainment and reasonable further progress or any other applicable requirement of the Clean Air Act (CAA or Act).”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the statutory standard for approving State Implementation Plan (SIP) revisions: EPA will approve SIP changes only if they do not interfere with attainment, reasonable further progress (RFP), or other applicable CAA requirements. Appears repeatedly as the threshold for EPA’s proposed/final approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attainment plan required elements (CAA)
rubrics_metrics.description: An attainment plan (for a NAA) includes the State's attainment demonstration and other elements required under the Clean Air Act: emission limitations necessary to provide for attainment; base-year and projection-year emission inventories; reasonably available control measures and reasonably available control technology (RACM/RACT); nonattainment new source review (NNSR); requirements for meeting reasonable further progress (RFP); and contingency measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating an attainment plan submittal, EPA looks for each of these specific elements. A SIP/attainment plan that lacks these components or does not adequately address them can be disapproved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional approval of SIP/local rule
rubrics_metrics.description: “EPA is proposing to conditionally approve a revision ... We are taking comments on this proposal and plan to follow with a final action.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA may issue conditional approvals of state/local measures subject to meeting specified conditions; such actions are announced for public comment and may be followed by a final approval or disapproval depending on whether conditions are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of authority to implement/enforce a federal plan
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA codified approval of a request for delegation of authority to implement and enforce the Federal plan for existing affected Sewage Sludge Incineration (SSI) units within a county. The Federal plan addresses implementation and enforcement of emission guidelines applicable in areas not covered by an approved state plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegations may be approved where a state/local agency demonstrates capability to implement a federal plan; the federal plan itself imposes emission limits and control requirements that the delegate must enforce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-informed, performance-based licensing standard for microreactors (NRC)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Proposing to amend its regulations to establish a risk-informed and performance-based regulatory framework for rapid licensing of new microreactors and other reactors with comparable risk profiles ... provide a flexible set of licensing pathways, reduce regulatory burden, and ensure that safety and security requirements remain commensurate with the potential hazards posed by these facilities.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensing criteria prioritize risk-informed and performance-based measures, flexibility for high-volume deployment, while maintaining safety/security proportional to hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Startup, shutdown, and malfunction SIP provisions must correct identified deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is proposing to approve SIP revisions that amend certain startup and shutdown provisions in a manner that avoids the deficiencies the EPA identified in a prior disapproval action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When states revise SIP provisions addressing SSM events, revisions must remedy previously-identified deficiencies to receive EPA approval (actions taken under CAA section 110).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attainment determinations may consider out‑of‑country emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may determine that an area would have attained the NAAQS by the attainment date but for emissions emanating from outside the United States (e.g., “would have attained ... but for emissions emanating from outside the United States”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA can account for international transport when deciding reclassification or attainment status; a finding that foreign emissions prevented attainment can affect classification and CAA obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial delegation of RMP (CAA 112(r)) with retained EPA authority
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA approved a state's request for partial delegation of Clean Air Act 112(r) Risk Management Program for agricultural anhydrous ammonia facilities, while retaining authority for anhydrous ammonia not meeting the agricultural definition and for other regulated chemicals/facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation can be partial and limited by chemical definitions or facility types; EPA may retain oversight and authority for matters outside the delegation scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably Available Control Technology (RACT) SIP requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: SIP revisions consist of regulations that implement statewide RACT requirements by limiting air emissions of oxides of nitrogen (NOx) from municipal waste combustors (MWCs) in the State; action is taken under the Clean Air Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must adopt enforceable RACT measures where applicable; EPA reviews SIPs for consistency with federal RACT obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic retention of Part 194 response plans permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule will amend facility response plan regulations to allow operators of oil pipelines to keep electronic copies of onshore oil spill response plans or the 'relevant portions' of those plans in lieu of paper copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory acceptance of electronic records may substitute for paper retention if the rule requirements (accessibility, integrity, availability) are satisfied; this reduces burden but requires compliance with any conditions set by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant New Use Rules (SNURs) — 90‑day pre-notification
rubrics_metrics.description: SNURs require persons to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing manufacture (including import) or processing of any chemical substance for an activity designated as a 'significant new use' in the SNUR. Manufacture/processing may not commence until EPA reviews the notification and takes appropriate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 90‑day PMN-like notification triggers EPA evaluation; regulated parties must await EPA determination before initiating the significant new use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory text must align with federal definitions (e.g., VOC)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is approving a SIP revision that amends the definition of volatile organic compound (VOC) in the State Administrative Code to align with the EPA's regulatory definition of VOC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State regulatory definitions should be consistent with applicable federal regulatory definitions where required by SIP or federal law to avoid inconsistency in implementation and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal area attainment findings and reclassification procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing its finding that tribal portions of an area did not attain the 2015 ozone NAAQS by the attainment date and reclassifying those portions to Serious nonattainment; EPA also acted on exceptional events requests submitted by the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA follows statutory procedures to determine attainment and may reclassify areas (including tribal portions) when attainment dates are not met; exceptional events requests and EPA concurrence/nonconcurrence are part of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan for existing MSW landfills under CAA section 111(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: A State Plan provides for implementation and enforcement of the Emissions Guidelines applicable to existing municipal solid waste landfills and establishes emission limits, monitoring, operating, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements for affected MSW landfills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be approvable, a state plan must contain enforceable requirements (limits, monitoring, O&M, recordkeeping, reporting) consistent with federal Emissions Guidelines and compliance times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pesticide tolerances must meet FFDCA and FIFRA registration review outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is finalizing tolerance actions under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FFDCA) that the Agency determined were necessary or appropriate during registration review under FIFRA; during registration review EPA reviews all aspects of a pesticide case, including existing tolerances, to ensure that the pesticide continues to meet the standard for registration under FIFRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tolerance actions follow from FIFRA registration review and must ensure tolerances are protective under FFDCA; EPA's registration review process evaluates whether continued registration is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: CAA section 112 technology review options for NESHAP
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA conducted a technology review pursuant to CAA section 112 and is considering two approaches for previously unregulated emission points: (1) determine EPA does not have an obligation to regulate them when conducting a 112(d)(6) review and defer action; or (2) propose new control standards for previously unregulated emission points. EPA also may propose minor technical corrections and changes to definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 112 technology reviews can result in no change, deferral, or new regulatory controls; EPA evaluates obligations under statute and may offer alternative regulatory approaches for public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction permit and fee updates must support NAAQS attainment/maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: State SIP revisions updating construction permit requirements (including fees, applicability thresholds, definitions, testing and reporting) must not interfere with the State's ability to attain or maintain the NAAQS, reasonable further progress (RFP) or other Clean Air Act requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative and fee changes are approvable only if they preserve the SIP's substantive ability to protect air quality and meet CAA obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attainment determinations based on certified monitoring and attainment-date extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may grant an attainment-date extension and determine attainment based on certified ozone monitoring data for specified years (e.g., 'determine that the area attained the 2015 ozone NAAQS based on certified ozone monitoring data from 2020-2022').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attainment status can hinge on certified monitoring records and approved extensions; states/tribes may request extensions and EPA evaluates monitoring data when reconsidering prior findings.
